_comment: DELIBERATELY PUBLIC. This read-write token is baked into the published page, so anyone who opens the lesson sheet can read, edit, or wipe these notes. That is the accepted trade for letting a tutor with no account take notes. Keep this database holding nothing but lesson notes, and treat the token as burned the moment it lands in git history — rotating it means issuing a new one, not removing this one. Turso's Delete Protection is on, but that only stops the database being deleted via the platform API; it does not stop 'drop table notes' over SQL.
schema: create table if not exists notes (week text not null, sentence_id text not null, note text not null default '', covered integer not null default 0, updated_at text not null, rev integer not null default 0, primary key (week, sentence_id))
create table if not exists week_notes (week text not null primary key, note text not null default '', updated_at text not null, rev integer not null default 0)
create table if not exists sentence_notes (sentence_id text not null primary key, note text not null default '', updated_at text not null, rev integer not null default 0)
_schema_note: Applied by hand against the live database, not by any code here — the page only ever reads and writes, never migrates. Add the DDL above before publishing a page that depends on it; all three statements are idempotent. WHAT LIVES WHERE: sentence_notes is the note, keyed by sentence and by nothing else, because what you worked out about a sentence is still true next month. notes is now only the weekly tick — its `note` column is vestigial, left populated so a browser still running the older page keeps showing something, and safe to blank once every client has reloaded. week_notes is the free-form pad for one week. rev is the compare-and-swap guard on all three: a write only lands if the row is still on the revision that browser last read, which is what makes it impossible to replace an edit you never saw. On a database predating it, add 'rev integer not null default 0' to each table; rows at rev 0 are accepted as an ancestor and move to 1 on the first edit.
